- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In low-sentiment (negative or near-zero) periods, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- If 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above true outcome, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 2% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average (mean reversion heuristic).
- When sentiment history shows strong recent volatility (e.g., ±0.3+ swings), reduce forecast smoothness and increase lag correction by 0.1–0.3 units per day.
